the physical vapor deposition of ZrO2 on Ti6Al4V alloy affects cell proliferation and osteoblastic differentiation of human osteoblasts.
zirconia layer on titanium surface influences cell behavior, but the influence depends on layer thickness.
the physical vapor deposition of ZrO2 onto Ti substrates affects the proliferation of primary osteoblast cells and their expression of BSP, ON and TGF- β in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical vapor deposition of ZrO2 on titanium and the influence of this process on the cell behavior.
the influence of surface chemistry, topography, and morphology of two novel titanium-based surfaces M2 and M1 on cell behavior of primary osteoblasts.
the preparation of novel surfaces with a different zirconia layer thickness, and with the characterization of these surfaces and their impact on cell proliferation and differentiation.

the physical vapour deposition of a zirconia layer on titanium surface is a promising technique to produce a surface with a different chemical and topographic composition.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the physical vapor deposition of a zirconia layer can be used to modify surface properties of titanium and that these properties may affect the osteoblast response.
the zirconia coating of titanium surfaces is a promising strategy in order to improve the surface properties of the latter and to increase the biocompatibility of the resulting materials.
the zirconia-based surfaces are biocompatible and can affect cell proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of osteoblasts in vitro.
